title: The husband who walked out in 1829
text: Ten years after Ludovicus Szathmáry left his wife Catharina Tóth and their four children, the church was still circulating his description across two dioceses: short, lean, pale, black-haired, a bad left eye, three languages besides his own. His wife's theory was that he got tired of home life and went back to the religion and the county he came from.

title: A seminarian goes missing
text: Franciscus Pap Vásárhelyi left the seminary on 21 May 1839 and did not come back. The vicar general asked every parish priest in the diocese to keep an eye out.

title: Priests skipping the district meeting
text: The May 1839 meeting at N. Kapos was so thinly attended that the vicar general demanded written excuses from every absentee.

title: Homework on kinship
text: The canon-law thesis for 1839 made every priest in the diocese explain stem, degree and line of consanguinity in writing. It is the same arithmetic this rebuild runs on.

title: A price list for sacraments
text: Parishioners complained about fees often enough that in February 1838 the bishop fixed one tariff for the whole diocese, from banns to funeral sermons, with weddings and burials priced by social standing.

title: The red silk veil
text: Between two diocesan circulars someone recorded a local event: on 25 August 1838 Miss Theresia Kulin gave the church a red silk veil worked with flowers. It is the only entry in the ten pages that was written about the parish itself.

title: Reading list by decree
text: The bishop doubled as a subscription agent: a Kassa bookseller's Hungarian edition of a French polemic on the Church of England, a Czech theological journal from Prague, a Pécs bishop's sermons. Each district was expected to buy at least one copy.

title: An underage wedding reaches Buda
text: A schoolmaster's son was married too young, the case went up to the Lieutenancy Council, and every parish got a reminder about the lawful age for marriage. Names in this entry are read with low confidence.

title: A Slovak form filled in Hungarian
text: The Belža entries survive as a later hand copy on a pre-printed Slovak form. The copyist ignored the printed headings, wrote Hungarian ones above them, and put legitimacy in the religion column and sex in the column meant for place of birth.

title: A village of boats and geese
text: From the Senné municipal history (lead L-012): when the rivers flooded, villagers dammed the hollows and took the fish as the water fell, and hunted deer and hares stranded on hummocks from dugout boats. Every family is said to have owned a boat into the interwar years, and the village goose flock ran to nearly six thousand birds until 1975.

title: A fisherman from Lake Constance
text: The same history says a Swiss fisherman was brought to Senné in the 1930s by the Sztáray family and introduced long seine nets to the marsh.

title: Twins, two crosses, and the name used again
text: György Demkó and Mária Hreskó had twin boys in May 1873, Mihály and János. Both names carry a cross in the register. The couple named a son János in 1875 and a son Mihály in 1882.

title: Two pages too early
text: Above the 1873 baptism of Mihály Hornyák the clerk admits the entry was written two pages ahead of where it belonged.

title: One register, three scripts
text: The same parish book is kept in Latin in 1831, Hungarian from 1834, and Cyrillic in 1857, when the priest of Lekárt entered a Viszoka baptism. The death note beside it, six weeks later, is back in Latin letters.

title: Baptised by the other rite, with permission
text: In 1831 Georgius Demko, son of a Greek Catholic father, was baptised by the Latin-rite parish priest of Pálóc, who noted that he had the consent of the local parish priest.

title: A seventeen-year-old gets his papers
text: The certificate that proves Štefan Duska's parents was issued at Senné on 19 August 1947, with a revenue stamp and the parish seal, when he was seventeen. Three years later his mother was buried in Montréal.

title: Alona, who was Anna
text: The owner filed the 1816 Krak baptism under the name Alona. The child in the entry is Anna.

title: András twice
text: János Kóreny and Mária Krak of Jesztreb baptised a son András in 1844 and another, entered in Cyrillic as Andrej, in 1852.

title: A date that corrects its own label
text: A file labelled "maybe 1876" carries a note that the child died on 27 February 1870, two days after the baptism.

title: The page header at last
text: After thirty-odd strips cut from the middle of pages, one includes the printed Hungarian headings of the register: running number, month and day of birth and of baptism, name, sex, legitimacy, parents' names with religion and standing, residence and house number, godparents, baptising priest, remarks.

title: Borbála twice, by two mothers
text: Pál Kocsis of Solymos baptised a Borbála in 1843 with Anna Cservenyák and another Borbála in 1846 with Mária Iv[a]ncsák. The simplest reading is a wife and a daughter lost within three years.

title: Twins need four godparents
text: The Demko twins of June 1877 at Jesztreb were given a pair of godparents each.
